predictions.title: Manipulable Curve spot quote directly controls NonUST share pricing
predictions.description: NonUSTStrategy.investedAssets values aUST and pending deposits by calling Curve.get_dy_underlying, a spot quote derived from pool state. Vault.totalUnderlying and totalUnderlyingMinusSponsored consume this value for deposit share minting, yield calculation, and withdrawals without a TWAP, deviation bound, or other manipulation resistance. An attacker can temporarily skew Curve reserves, call Vault.deposit while the quote is depressed to receive excess shares, restore the pool price, and later withdraw those shares for more underlying than deposited.
predictions.impact: The attacker can obtain an excessive share balance and drain underlying from the vault, diluting existing depositors and potentially causing substantial loss of vault assets.
predictions.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant valuation such as a bounded TWAP or independently verified oracle, enforce deviation and liquidity checks, and avoid allowing deposits or withdrawals when the valuation is outside configured bounds or changes abnormally within a transaction.

predictions.title: Zero-output protection allows Curve price manipulation to steal strategy assets during swaps
predictions.description: NonUSTStrategy converts underlying to UST and UST back to underlying using Curve exchange_underlying with min_dy set to zero. The reverse conversion is invoked by the permissionless finishRedeemStable path after asynchronous redemption. An attacker can manipulate Curve immediately before settlement, trigger finishRedeemStable, and force the strategy to accept an arbitrarily poor exchange rate, with no transaction-level slippage protection.
predictions.impact: Redeemed UST can be converted into materially less underlying than expected, permanently reducing strategy assets and the value recoverable by vault depositors.
predictions.mitigation: Compute a trusted expected output immediately before the swap and pass a conservative min_dy with an explicit slippage limit. Add price-impact, pool-liquidity, and oracle-deviation checks, and restrict or otherwise safely coordinate permissionless settlement so a caller cannot settle during an observable manipulated state.
